questions.q: Why does the methodology section of the write-up need the exact benchmark command, not just the final numbers?
options: So the results are reproducible rather than numbers a reader just has to take on faith
Because the executive summary section is not allowed to contain numbers
It's a formatting requirement with no practical benefit
So the model's license terms can be verified
questions.explain: Including the exact model, framework, hardware, and benchmark command lets someone else reproduce the results rather than simply trusting a quoted number.

questions.q: Why does the write-up explicitly name the deployment as a single point of failure, rather than leaving that detail out?
options: Because a write-up that hides its remaining risk is worse than one with no write-up, since it creates a false sense of completeness
Because every write-up is legally required to list every possible failure
Because the deployment is actually broken and unusable
Because autoscaling has already been added and this is just a historical note
questions.explain: Naming the open risk honestly — a single-GPU deployment with no redundancy yet — lets the reader make a real decision instead of acting on a false sense of completeness.

questions.q: Why was Mixtral 8x7B listed in the write-up as 'considered, rejected' rather than left out entirely?
options: Because it was never a real candidate in Lesson 34
Because showing what was considered and why it was rejected (GPU budget, not quality) is part of an honest trade-off discussion
Because Mixtral 8x7B does not exist as an open-weight model
Because the write-up format forbids mentioning rejected options
questions.explain: An honest write-up documents the alternatives that were weighed and why they were set aside, so a reader can judge whether the reasoning still holds for their situation.

questions.q: Which is the correct order of the four courses in the AI Infrastructure / ML Systems Engineer destination?
options: Inference & Model Serving, GPU Computing, ML Infrastructure & Platform Engineering, Distributed Training Infrastructure
GPU Computing, Distributed Training Infrastructure, ML Infrastructure & Platform Engineering, Inference & Model Serving
ML Infrastructure & Platform Engineering, GPU Computing, Inference & Model Serving, Distributed Training Infrastructure
Distributed Training Infrastructure, Inference & Model Serving, GPU Computing, ML Infrastructure & Platform Engineering
questions.explain: The destination goes hardware (GPU Computing), then the systems view of training at scale (Distributed Training Infrastructure), then the platform layer (ML Infrastructure & Platform Engineering), then the serving layer that closes it (Inference & Model Serving).

questions.q: What does completing this capstone and this lesson mean for the AI Infrastructure / ML Systems Engineer destination?
options: There are three more courses still required before the destination is complete
The destination is now complete — all four courses, from raw hardware to a benchmarked, defensible serving endpoint, form one provable path
This lesson only completes the course, and a separate capstone course is still required for the destination
The destination has no defined ending point
questions.explain: This lesson closes both the course and the full four-course AI Infrastructure / ML Systems Engineer destination, which this capstone project ties together end to end.
